issues.display_title: Issue #611: Add Panorama: building-scoped import with virtual-tour floor mapping
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Add Panorama imports panoramas from a virtual tour and places them on a project. In a project with more than one building that is not safe: the import experience never states which building is being edited, and a multi-floor tour carries several floors with no way to say which tour floor belongs to which project floor. Panoramas land on the wrong floor, or in the wrong building entirely — the failure mode for campus, mall, hospital, and multi-building commercial projects.

RESULT

Branch: design/add-panorama-building-scoped

Scope the import to the active building, and make the floor pairing an explicit choice instead of a silent guess.

PRD: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-10-add-panorama-building-floor-mapping/prd.md
Brief: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-10-add-panorama-building-floor-mapping/brief.md

Scope

Match Floors — a step both import actions pass through

  • Shows the active building by name (Importing into: Main Building) plus a count summary (3 building floors, 3 virtual-tour floors detected).
  • One row per building floor, ground floor first, active building only. Floors from other buildings never appear and never receive panoramas.
  • Each row picks one virtual-tour floor from a dropdown. Options are two-line: floor name on top, 14 panoramas below — or Already selected for a floor another row has taken, which stays visible but unpickable so the reason is legible.
  • No virtual tour floor clears a row and frees the option again.
  • Default pairing is by order; surplus floors on either side stay unmapped rather than doubling up.
  • Unmapped tour floors are named before Apply and are skipped on import. Confirm is disabled until at least one floor is mapped.
  • A single-floor tour skips the step entirely — nothing to choose (R14).

Routing

  • Floor routing moves off the positional floorConfigs[pano.level] lookup, which reached across the whole project and could not be corrected by the user, onto a mapping keyed by active-building level ids. That is what makes cross-building import impossible rather than merely unlikely.
  • Projects with no Building record keep the existing default-building behaviour and read as Main Building.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Import is scoped to the active building; floors of other buildings are never written to
  • Existing default-building behaviour still works when no building record exists
  • The modal shows the active building name
  • Only active-building floors appear in the mapping UI
  • Virtual-tour floors appear in dropdowns with readable labels, no raw ids
  • Default mapping is created by order
  • Users can change the mapping before applying
  • A virtual-tour floor cannot be assigned to two building floors
  • Changing or clearing a selection frees the tour floor again
  • Unmapped virtual-tour floors are skipped, and the UI says so before Apply
  • Apply still completes when at least one floor is mapped
  • Single-floor tours remain simple — no extra step
  • Existing virtual-tour link entry and tour loading are unchanged
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

New

  • src/components/editor/add-panorama/floorMapping.ts — the whole rule set as pure functions: detectTourFloors, buildingFloors, activeBuildingName, defaultFloorMapping, assignTourFloor (one-to-one), unmappedTourFloors, fallbackLevelId.
  • src/components/editor/add-panorama/MatchFloorsStep.tsx — the mapping UI.
  • src/components/editor/add-panorama/MatchFloorsModal.tsx — dialog chrome, shared by both import actions.
  • src/components/editor/add-panorama/__tests__/floorMapping.test.ts — 18 tests over R2/R3/R4/R7/R8/R12/R13/R14.
  • src/app/design-preview/pano-floor-mapping/page.tsx — design preview with static data, so the mapping UI can be reviewed without a multi-floor tour.
  • docs/.../access-flow.md — access flow, four paths, QA checklist.

Changed

  • placeMarkers.ts — groupPanosByLevel takes a FloorMapping keyed by active-building level ids instead of a positional index across the whole project. Unmapped tour floors are dropped rather than guessed. Both callers route through here, so one change covers both import paths.
  • ApplyLocationModal.tsx — building-scoped, persistent Importing into chip, floor tabs from the confirmed mapping, Back to revise it.
  • AddPanoramaModal.tsx — Match Floors hoisted above the Import / Import & Apply Location split.
  • AddPanoramaButton.tsx — plain Import is building-scoped too.
  • useFloorPlanLayer.ts — isLive(map) guard replacing bare if (!map). A remove()d map keeps responding but has torn its style down, so getSource throws; the dialog now unmounts and re-mounts its map (Back), and StrictMode does the same on every dev mount.

Notes

  • Plain Import also stops at Match Floors for a multi-floor tour. Placing on a guessed floor is the failure this issue exists to prevent; skipping the ask only makes it fail quietly.
  • Panoramas without location data are mapped before being placed, so they land on the same floors as their located siblings.
  • Match Floors only appears for tours whose overlay carries map.multiple_map_data (TourMkr multi-floor Floor Map) — that is the only parser branch that stamps pano.level. Lat/lng tours are single-floor by definition and go straight through, which is correct, but worth knowing when preparing test data.

issues.display_title: Issue #604: Editor Map: outer buildings and scoped placement tools
issues.main_description_html:
Editor Map mode must stay understandable when a project contains more than one building.

Today the active building and the surrounding buildings are not visually separated enough, so users lose spatial context while editing. Placement tools also do not say what they will change, so a user can move a floor when they meant a building — or move one building when they expected all of them.

Brief: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-07-editor-map-outer-buildings-scoped-tools/brief.md
PRD: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-07-editor-map-outer-buildings-scoped-tools/prd.md

Scope

1. Outer buildings (R1–R14)

  • The selected building always renders indoors. Editor Map mode has no Overview mode and never shows every building as outer-only.
  • Every non-selected building renders as an outer shell with its building name.
  • Shells hide all indoor detail: rooms, walls, markers, shapes, safety annotations, panorama markers, indoor labels.
  • Existing empty-state behaviour is preserved for buildings without usable floor geometry.

2. Click-to-select (R15–R22)

  • Clicking a non-selected outer building selects it; it becomes the indoor building and the previous one becomes a shell.
  • The building selector and active floor follow the new selection.
  • Clicking empty map space, or the already-selected building, changes nothing.
  • In drag mode a click on another building's shell selects only — the same gesture must not drag it.

3. Scoped placement tools (R23–R38)

Exactly three user-facing scopes, applied consistently to drag, rotate, scale, move and reset:

Scope Target
All Buildings Every building together — relative positions preserved
Selected Building The active building only
Selected Floor The active floor only
  • Each scope's reset clears only its own placement frame.
  • Tooltips and move-mode hints name the active scope.
  • "Project" is not exposed as a fourth scope.

Out of scope

Preview and live project behaviour · viewer-facing Overview mode · building add/rename/delete · floor create/rename/delete/reorder · persistence, backend APIs, DB fields, permissions, billing, analytics · outdoor routing.

Acceptance

  • Selected building stays active indoors; non-selected buildings render as named outer shells
  • Shells hide indoor detail
  • No Overview mode, and never an all-outer state
  • Clicking a shell selects that building; selector and active floor follow
  • Empty-map clicks change nothing; drag mode selects first without dragging
  • Scopes are exactly All Buildings / Selected Building / Selected Floor
  • Drag, rotate, scale, move and reset all respect the active scope
  • Tooltips and hints name the active scope
  • Preview and live project behaviour unchanged

RESULT

Branch: design/editor-map-outer-buildings
